<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
**Plan draft — by `kimi-k3:medium@claudex`** (headless Claude Code harness via local proxy, read-only allowlist; harness is part of the measurement).

# Plan — TKT-70: pre-clean smoke stack before `compose up`

## 1. DoD (mapped to COS)

**COS:** the smoke run cannot start from a dirty volume.

| # | Done criterion | How observed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `compose down -v --remove-orphans` runs **before** `compose up -d --build --wait` in `scripts/smoke.sh` on every invocation (fast path and `SMOKE_HERMETIC=1`), unconditionally | Code inspection; `bash -x ./scripts/smoke.sh` shows the `down` before `up` |
| 2 | A dirty-volume reproduction no longer passes silently: after seeding a stale `pgdata` under the smoke project (run smoke, `kill -9` it mid-run so the trap can't fire, leaving the volume), the next `./scripts/smoke.sh` run tears it down and migrates from empty | Manual scripted repro run before/after (see §3) |
| 3 | The pre-clean cannot tear down a *sibling* worktree's running smoke stack | Project name is per-checkout (`ticketing-smoke-$SLOT`, SLOT hashed from `$ROOT`, `smoke.sh:26-27`) — `down -v` is scoped to `-p "$PROJECT"`, which is unique per worktree; verified by reading lines 26–27, no new mechanism |
| 4 | Trap-based cleanup on EXIT/INT/TERM stays | Unchanged line 57 |
| 5 | `make check` still passes end-to-end | `make check` locally, CI `check.yaml` green |

## 2. Files to touch

**One file: `scripts/smoke.sh`** — insert one line between the trap (line 57) and the `compose up` (line 59):

```bash
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

# Pre-clean: a hard-killed previous run (SIGKILL, crashed daemon, killed CI
# runner) left its volumes behind; without this, `compose up` would reuse the
# already-migrated pgdata and the gate would "prove" the clean-clone bootstrap
# against a schema an earlier run applied — silently voiding
# TestMigrationsAppliedOutOfBand (ADR-022).
compose down -v --remove-orphans >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

if ! compose up -d --build --wait; then
```

Reuse the existing `cleanup` function instead if preferred — `cleanup` *is* exactly this command (`smoke.sh:56`), so calling `cleanup` inline before `up` is the one-word diff. Either form is one line; calling `cleanup` avoids duplicating the flags. Recommendation: **call `cleanup`**.

```bash
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
# Pre-clean: a hard-killed previous run (SIGKILL, crashed daemon, killed CI
# runner) left its volumes behind; without this, `compose up` would reuse the
# already-migrated pgdata and the gate would "prove" the clean-clone bootstrap
# against a schema an earlier run applied (ADR-022).
cleanup
```

No other files. Makefile, CI workflows, compose files, Go tests — all untouched. Migrations stay exactly where ADR-022 puts them (one-shot compose jobs); this change only guarantees they run against an empty volume.

## 3. Test plan — named seam and honest red-first assessment

**Named seam:** the `cleanup` shell function at `scripts/smoke.sh:56`, invoked at line ~58 (new call site) vs. line 57 (trap). The behavior under test is ordering: `down` must precede `up`.

**Red-first automated test — impractical; stating so explicitly.** A true red-first automated test would have to (a) stand up the real compose stack, (b) SIGKILL the script mid-run, (c) assert the volume survives, (d) re-run and assert the new run doesn't reuse it. That is a multi-minute, Docker-daemon-dependent scenario that cannot live in `make check`'s unit-test stages, and scripting it into CI would make the gate test itself with a flaky SIGKILL timing race. The repo has no bash test framework and this ticket does not justify one. `scripts/gate-selftest.sh` (the repo's existing mechanism for proving the gate catches seeded errors) targets *Make stages* with seeded source errors — a trap-ordering defect is not expressible as a seeded source error, so the self-test seam doesn't fit either.

**Closest verifiable substitute — scripted dirty-volume repro, run once before and once after the change:**

```bash
# 1. Start a smoke run and hard-kill it once postgres is up and migrated,
#    before the trap can fire. Leaving the project volume behind.
./scripts/smoke.sh & SMOKE_PID=$!
sleep 60   # until `compose up --wait` reports healthy; adjust by observation
kill -9 $SMOKE_PID
# trap cannot run on SIGKILL — volume `ticketing-smoke-<slot>_pgdata` survives:
docker volume ls | grep "ticketing-smoke-.*pgdata"   # MUST show the volume

# 2. Re-run smoke. BEFORE the change: `compose up` reuses the migrated pgdata
#    (visible in migrate-job logs as "no migrations to apply" / goose version
#    already at latest). AFTER the change: the pre-clean removes the volume
#    first; migrate jobs log applying migrations from version 0.
./scripts/smoke.sh 2>&1 | tee /tmp/smoke-after.log
grep -E 'migrate|goose' /tmp/smoke-after.log   # AFTER: migrations applied fresh
docker volume ls | grep "ticketing-smoke-.*pgdata"   # gone by run end (trap)
```

The red/green signal is in the migrate-job logs (`docker compose -p ticketing-smoke-<slot> logs catalog-migrate` etc.): **before** the change they report the schema already at latest on the second run; **after**, they report applying the full chain. That is exactly the assertion `TestMigrationsAppliedOutOfBand` (`smoke/smoke_test.go:277`) cannot make on its own against a stale volume — the repro is the test.

**Gate regression check:** full `make check` passes after the change (the extra `down` is a no-op on a clean runner, so CI behavior is unchanged).

## 4. Risks / pre-mortem

| Risk | Assessment | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **Pre-clean tears down a concurrently running sibling worktree's stack** | **No.** Project name is `ticketing-smoke-$SLOT` with SLOT = `cksum($ROOT) % 40` (`smoke.sh:26-27`) — each worktree gets its own project, and `down` is scoped by `-p "$PROJECT"`. The header comment (lines 12–25) documents this as load-bearing for exactly this reason. A `SMOKE_COMPOSE_PROJECT` override shared between two runs would collide — but that's true of the existing trap today (documented at lines 14–18), and the override exists precisely to take that responsibility. | None needed; verify by reading lines 26–27 (done). |
| **Extra `down` cost on every run** | `docker compose down -v` against a non-existent project is sub-second (no containers, no volumes, one API round-trip). Against a leftover stack it adds the teardown time the trap would have paid anyway. | Non-issue. |
| **`SMOKE_COMPOSE_PROJECT` override interaction** | The override flows through the same `compose()` wrapper, so pre-clean honors it identically to the trap. No new behavior. | None. |
| **CI behavior** | CI runners start clean, so the pre-clean is a no-op there; `check.yaml` needs no change. The one case it changes CI semantics is a *reused* self-hosted runner with leftover volumes — which is precisely the defect being fixed. | None. |
| **`down` fails partway (daemon hiccup) leaving partial state** | `|| true` swallows the error and `compose up` proceeds — same failure mode as today's trap. The subsequent `compose up --wait` failing on port/volume conflict is the honest failure the header comment already accepts. | Acceptable; matches existing error posture. |
| **Someone later moves the pre-clean *after* the artifact checks** | Artifact checks (lines 39–46) exit before the trap is even installed in the current order — a pre-clean placed there would still run, since `cleanup` runs before them regardless of position relative to the trap line. Placement between trap and `up` is the only ordering that matters. | One-line comment at the call site states why it must precede `up`. |

## 5. Explicitly out of scope

- **TKT-69 (port collision)** — separate ticket; this plan does not touch port allocation, SLOT derivation, or the `export GATEWAY_PORT …` block.
- No changes to where/how migrations run (ADR-022 governs; the one-shot compose jobs stay).
- No bash test framework, no new CI job, no Makefile target — the repro script in §3 is a one-time manual verification, not a committed artifact (unless the implementer wants to drop it under `scripts/` — not recommended; it can't run in CI reliably).

---

**Summary of the whole change:** in `scripts/smoke.sh`, add one call — `cleanup` — between the trap and `compose up`, with a comment explaining why. The trap keeps handling the normal path; the pre-clean closes the SIGKILL/daemon-crash/killed-runner hole that let `TestMigrationsAppliedOutOfBand` pass against schema an earlier run applied.

Skipped: automated trap-ordering test (impractical — stated in §3, scripted before/after repro is the substitute); committed repro script (can't run in CI reliably). Add when: the repo adopts a bash test seam or smoke-stage self-test harness.

**Plan critique (planReview: `main-agent`) + finalization — delta over the kind=plan draft.**

**Verified against HEAD:** `cleanup`/trap/`compose up` at `scripts/smoke.sh:56/57/59` ✓; `TestMigrationsAppliedOutOfBand` at `smoke/smoke_test.go:277` (draft said 277 ✓); per-worktree project isolation `smoke.sh:26-27` ✓; `pgdata` is a compose-declared named volume (`compose.yaml:345-346`) ✓; `scripts/gate-selftest.sh` exists ✓. No hallucinated seams.

**Accepted:** DoD, the one-file diff, calling `cleanup` (not duplicating the flags) between trap and `compose up`, the pre-mortem rows on sibling-worktree safety / cost / `SMOKE_COMPOSE_PROJECT` / CI, and the out-of-scope list (TKT-69 untouched, no bash test framework, repro script not committed).

**Amended:**
1. **§3 red repro** — the draft's SIGKILL-mid-run repro depends on a `sleep 60` timing guess and two full smoke runs. Replaced with a deterministic seeding repro: `compose up -d postgres` (seconds), write a marker file into the compose-created `pgdata` volume, `docker kill` the postgres container (simulating the hard-killed run — trap never fires, volume survives), then start `./scripts/smoke.sh` and observe the marker. **Red (pre-fix):** marker still present once the new run's postgres is up — the dirty volume leaked into the run. **Green (post-fix):** marker gone within seconds of script start (pre-clean removed the volume). Run killed with INT after observation (trap cleans); full `make check` at the end regardless.
2. **§4 last pre-mortem row** — the draft's reasoning about placement vs the artifact checks is garbled (the trap is installed *after* those checks, and `cleanup` does not run before them "regardless of position"). Replaced with the simple rule: the pre-clean sits between the trap install and `compose up`; the call-site comment pins the ordering.

**Rejected:** none.

**Self-made decisions (Gate 2 waived by repo owner — recorded per the waiver):**
- Form of the fix: call `cleanup` inline (draft's own recommendation).
- Repro script not committed (draft's recommendation; also the most reversible choice).
- Red-first TDD satisfied via the observed-red seeding repro, since an automated trap-ordering test is impractical (draft §3's argument, accepted).

**Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model:** the deterministic seeded-marker repro design (amendment 1). Everything else is the draft, as amended above — **the kind=plan draft as amended here is the plan.**

Unmodified script: marker survived into the next run → **red observed**. Fixed script, same seeding: marker gone within seconds of start, new postgres migrated from empty → **green observed**. **Per-finding verdicts (checked against branch HEAD):**
1. *"Blocking": volume-only pre-clean would reuse Exited-0 migrate containers* — **reclassified minor, fixed**. By the finding's own analysis the shipped code is correct (`cleanup` runs the full `down`, removing containers *and* volumes); the defect exists only if a future refactor narrows the pre-clean to volume removal. The comment now states the full `down` is load-bearing and why (commit 90f36b2).
2. *Pre-clean swallows a dead Docker daemon* — **rejected**: pre-existing error posture (the trap and `compose up` behave identically today), accepted in plan-final's pre-mortem; the added comment makes no liveness claim to soften. No behavior change.
3. *Comment overstates the silent case* — **accepted, fixed**: now says *same-revision* pgdata; an older checkout's schema fails the version assertion loudly (90f36b2).

**Second pass: not run** — the fix diff is comment-only (7 insertions/4 deletions, zero logic), which is the pure-trivia case; one pass, recorded here per the skill's rule.

1. **Pre-clean exists and is ordered correctly** — `scripts/smoke.sh` calls `cleanup` (full `compose down -v --remove-orphans`, project-scoped) between the trap install and `compose up`.
2. **Behavioral proof (red/green on the branch, same code as merged)** — seeded `pgdata` with a marker and `docker kill`ed postgres so the trap never fired: unmodified script reused the dirty volume (marker visible inside the next run); fixed script wiped it before `up` (fresh migration from empty).

description:
**Found by TKT-66** (and independently by the Codex plan draft on that ticket).

`scripts/smoke.sh:26-29`:

```bash
compose() { docker compose -p "$PROJECT" "${COMPOSE_FILES[@]}" "$@"; }
cleanup() { compose down -v --remove-orphans >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM
if ! compose up -d --build --wait; then ...
```

Teardown runs **only** on the exit trap. A hard-killed run (SIGKILL, a crashed daemon, a reboot, a
killed CI runner) leaves the volumes behind, and the next `compose up` reuses the already-migrated
`pgdata`. The gate then passes without ever proving the **clean-clone bootstrap** it claims to prove
— `make check` from a clean clone is a stated repo invariant (`AGENTS.md`), and this is the one place
that would catch a migration chain that only works on a pre-existing database.

Now more load-bearing than before: since [ADR-021](docs/adr/ADR-021-out-of-band-service-migrations.md)
migrations run in one-shot jobs, and `TestMigrationsAppliedOutOfBand` asserts each database is at its
latest checked-in version. Against a stale volume that assertion can pass on schema an earlier run
applied, not this one.

**COS:** the smoke run cannot start from a dirty volume — e.g. pre-clean (`down -v --remove-orphans`)
*before* `compose up`, not only in the trap. Cheap; the trap stays for the normal path.

**Not in scope:** the port-collision defect (TKT-69).
